notes: Company: B2B marketing platform that auto-generates multi-variant email campaigns and dynamic landing pages.
Primary pain: per-campaign token costs are unpredictable. High volume of short, template-driven prompts (emails, CTAs, subject lines).
Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable unit economics — if cost spikes we have to turn LLM off across thousands of customers.'
Interested in hosted_api for fast time-to-value and self-serve onboarding; likely to remain on public cloud for at least 6-12 months.
Key technical asks: transparent per-route token breakdown, prefix/KV caching across campaign templates, batching for embeddings jobs, model/quantization recommendations for cost tradeoffs.

Throughput/latency targets: bursty writes at campaign publish (avg 200rps bursts), typical gen latency target <800ms for user preview; background embeddings pipeline tolerant to higher latency but cost-sensitive.
Estimated volume: initial POC sim of ~300k tokens/day; growth plan targets 1M+ tokens/day in 3-6 months if costs are favorable.
Cost sensitivity high: wants suggestions: caching identical template prefixes, batching embeddings (site search), smaller cheaper model families for most tasks, and Optimize recommendations.
Security: require SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration for admin access, audit logs for customer data exports; data residency not required today.
POC scope agreed: 2-week test with sample tenancy of 10k users, measure cost per campaign, latency p95, cache hit rate; deliverables: POC report + recommended config for batching/kv cache.
Sales notes: keep messaging simple — emphasize predictable billing, caching primitives, per-route analytics, and low-friction hosted onboarding.
Potential expansion: Dedicated reserved capacity in 12-18 months if volume ramps and they need tighter latency SLAs or data isolation.
Open questions: exact billing cadence (monthly vs committed), rate-limit burst policy, SDK language support for their Node.js microservices.
Blocker summary: waiting on clarifications in pricing deck and final security docs before enabling POC credentials.
